query: Whether penal interest can be capitalized or compounded by NBFCs / Banks in SARFAESI proceedings?
title: Central Bank of India vs Ravindra & Ors (Constitution Bench 2002 1 SCC 367) r.w. RBI Circular 2023
plainEnglish: A Constitution Bench held that penal interest is charged only by way of penalty for default and cannot be capitalized or compounded with the principal debt. The 2023 RBI circular explicitly mandates that lenders cannot levy penal interest in the form of compounded interest.
whyItMatters: Crucial defense against Coastal Finance's LN-002 claim of ₹ 42.10 Cr. Meridian has legitimate grounds to expunge ₹ 3.50 Cr of compounded penal interest from the demand notice.

query: Pre-existing dispute threshold under Section 8 and Section 9 of IBC 2016 for operational debt rejection
title: Mobilox Innovations Pvt Ltd vs Kirusa Software Pvt Ltd
plainEnglish: The Supreme Court ruled that an adjudicating authority (NCLT) must reject an operational creditor's Section 9 petition if there exists a plausible contention of dispute raised prior to the demand notice under Section 8. The dispute need not be proven conclusively at the admission stage.
whyItMatters: Directly supports Meridian Infra Holdings in M-2026-003 against Zenith Infra Projects. Meridian raised written quality objections on defective steel on 12 Dec 2025, one month before Zenith issued its Section 8 notice.

query: Section 4 Ryotwari Patta under Andhra Pradesh / Telangana Inams Abolition Act 1956 overriding pre-1950 Inam claims
court: High Court for the State of Telangana
title: B. Ramulu & Ors vs State of Telangana & Ors
plainEnglish: Once an Occupancy Rights Certificate (ORC) or Ryotwari Patta is granted by the Inams Tribunal under Section 4 of the 1956 Act and attains finality, civil suits seeking partition based on pre-abolition Inam grants are barred by limitation and res judicata.
whyItMatters: Direct defense in Matter M-2025-021 for Sunrise Developers against the legal heirs of Mirza Asad Baig regarding Survey 89/2.
